transcript: June starting, move officially two weeks out now, packing continuing in the background of everything else. Meridian work steady and genuinely enjoyable most days, still can't quite believe how different it feels from the Atlas grind. Warm evening, sat on the balcony for a while before bed, small quiet moment before the busy weeks ahead.

Realized today how much is actually left to sort before the move, way more than I estimated, and had a small stress spiral about the timeline this evening, boxes everywhere, half the kitchen still not packed. Deep breath. It'll get done, it always does, but tonight it felt like a lot all at once.

Pottery Thursday, took a break from packing to make it and glad I did, needed the reset. Told the class this is one of my last sessions here since the new apartment's a bit far for the Thursday commute, might look for a studio closer once I'm settled. Bittersweet thought, this class has meant more to me this year than I expected when I nervously signed up back in January.

More packing, methodically working through the closets now. Found an old photo of Nonna in a box of odds and ends, sat with it for a minute before carefully wrapping it to move safely. Small moment, kept it brief tonight, tired from the boxes.

Early run before another day of packing chaos, needed the movement to clear my head before diving back into boxes. Summer mornings genuinely lovely now, warm but not yet oppressive, good light. Legs still feeling strong from half marathon training, keeping easy mileage up during the move stress instead of dropping it entirely.

Kitchen fully packed now, living room half done. Dario coming this weekend to help with the big stuff, grateful to have him now on the giving-help side after he needed it back in May. Funny how this year turned that around.

Dario came by today to help load some of the bigger furniture into a rented truck ahead of next weekend's actual move, good practice run for moving day itself. Easy between us again the way it was helping him move back in May, boxes and bad jokes and neither of us needing to make it more meaningful than it already quietly is.

Exhausted from the weekend's furniture wrangling, whole body sore in new places. Last full Sunday in this apartment, sat for a while in the mostly-empty living room just letting myself feel a little sentimental about the place, first apartment I really made mine, a lot happened here this year, good and hard both.

Final week at the old place, work at Meridian still steady, trying to focus there despite the move looming over everything. Last few boxes to go, mostly just the essentials I'll need until moving day itself now.

Signed the final paperwork on the new place today, officially official now, keys in hand as of this weekend. Strange mix of nerves and excitement, a fresh space feels like it means something bigger this year than just square footage, feels like a small physical marker of everything that's shifted since January.

Picked up the keys this evening, walked through the empty new apartment by myself for a few minutes before telling anyone, just wanted a quiet first look. Bigger than I remembered from the viewing, good light in the late afternoon, kitchen window already promising a decent view once I'm actually living with it day to day. Real move is this weekend.

Last few days of packing, down to the very last odds and ends now. Movers booked for Sunday. Nervous energy building but also just ready for this to be over honestly, packing takes more out of you than people give it credit for.

Second to last pottery session at this particular studio, felt more emotional than I expected walking out tonight, said proper goodbyes to a couple of the regulars I've gotten to know this year. Going to miss this specific room, the specific light in it on Thursday evenings, even though pottery itself isn't going anywhere for me, just this particular space.

Last night in the old apartment, sleeping on a mattress on the floor since the bed frame's already loaded in the truck. Strange feeling, echo-y empty rooms, all my stuff either gone or in boxes by the door. Tomorrow's the actual move. Ready for it, genuinely, even with the small sentimental pang tonight.

Moved into the new place today, Fremont, finally. Whole day a blur of boxes, sweat, and Dario and Maya and Tom all pitching in with the heavy stuff while I directed traffic mostly badly. Exhausted in every part of my body right now, the specific exhaustion of an entire day of physical labor, but genuinely happy underneath it, that good tired that comes with something actually finished. Standing in the kitchen just now doing dishes before collapsing into bed, I looked up and caught the view out the window for real for the first time properly, not just the quick glance from the walkthrough, the canal catching the last of the evening light, a couple of people walking a dog along the path. Small unexpected gift, this window. Going to enjoy mornings here I think. First night in a new place, boxes everywhere still, but it already feels like it could be home.

First full day in the new place, unpacking chaos everywhere still, boxes labeled in ways that made sense a week ago and now mean nothing. Found the coffee maker at least, priorities. Slept fine actually despite the new noises, different street sounds, a boat horn from the canal at one point that startled me awake briefly before I remembered where I was.

More unpacking, slowly getting the place into some kind of order. Went for a walk along the canal in the evening, first proper exploration of the new neighborhood, nice little coffee shop a few blocks down I want to try this weekend.

Meridian work resuming full focus now that the move's mostly settled, good to have that steady rhythm back after weeks of packing chaos interrupting everything. Apartment starting to feel less like a construction site and more like an actual home, most boxes unpacked now, just the art and small decor stuff left.

First run from the new place this morning, discovered a whole stretch of canal path I didn't know existed, quiet and shaded by trees for a good chunk of it, might become my new regular route. Small joy in discovering a new neighborhood through running, learning it with your legs instead of just a map.

First pottery class at a new studio closer to the new apartment, different vibe than the old place, smaller, quieter, fewer people but a nice instructor who complimented my technique right away which was a confidence boost after feeling like a beginner all over again in an unfamiliar room. Going to take some adjusting but I think this could work out.

Prepping for Dario's birthday dinner tomorrow, picked up a gift, a little nervous honestly about hosting since it's my first real gathering in the new place. Want it to go well, feels like it matters more than a normal dinner given everything this year.

Dario's birthday dinner tonight, first time hosting in the new place and it went better than I let myself hope for. Cooked way too much food, classic overcompensating, but nobody minded the leftovers. At some point in the evening he brought up this ridiculous memory from when we were kids, the time we tried to build a treehouse with zero actual carpentry skills and it collapsed the very first time either of us climbed into it, Dad laughing so hard he had to sit down on the grass. We were both laughing so hard retelling it that I had actual tears, the kind of laugh that comes from somewhere deep and old, the specific laugh only a sibling can pull out of you because they were actually there for the stupid thing in the first place. Sitting there afterward, dishes still on the table, I had this quiet realization that the repair between us isn't fragile anymore, isn't something we're carefully managing around, it's just real again, ordinary and real, the way it used to be before everything. Best birthday dinner I think I've ever thrown, and it wasn't even mine.

Recovering from last night's hosting, dishes finally all put away today. Still smiling thinking about the treehouse story, going to remember that laugh for a long time I think. Quiet Sunday otherwise, needed the rest after the social energy of yesterday.

Mundane Tuesday, work steady at Meridian, canal walk in the evening becoming a real habit now, good way to decompress after a full day. Started glazing a few pieces at the new studio, curious how the different kiln here will change the colors compared to the old place.

Thinking about the street market this weekend, Maya mentioned she has a booth and encouraged me to consider selling some pottery there myself if I had enough pieces built up. Nervous about the idea honestly, feels different putting something you made out for strangers to judge with their wallets, but also a little exciting. Going to look through what I have tonight and see if there's actually enough decent stuff.

Morning run along the canal again, this route genuinely becoming my favorite of anywhere I've lived, quiet and green and the water catching the early light beautifully most mornings. Legs strong, good energy heading into a busy weekend of pricing and prepping pottery pieces for the market.

Spent the evening pricing pottery pieces for the weekend market, harder than expected to put a number on something you made with your own hands, kept second guessing every price. Landed on a handful I'm actually proud enough of to sell. Nervous but committed now.

Wrapping and packing the market pieces carefully tonight so nothing chips on the way there tomorrow. Maya's walking me through the whole booth setup process since she's done it before. Weirdly nervous about this, more than a normal work presentation somehow, probably because it's so personal, my actual hands on every single piece.

Set up the booth alongside Maya's this evening ahead of tomorrow's market, laid out the pieces, a little proud actually seeing them all together like that, a whole little collection of things that started as shapeless clay months ago. Early start tomorrow. Trying to manage my expectations, will be happy if even one thing sells.

Sold two pieces at the market today. Two. A complete stranger, a woman about my mom's age, picked up the blue bowl, the one from back in February that I made not long after Nonna died, turned it over in her hands, asked if I'd made it myself, and then just bought it, handed over actual money for a thing that came out of my own hands. I don't think I've ever felt anything quite like that particular flavor of joy, completely disproportionate to two bowls and maybe sixty dollars, but it wasn't really about the money at all. It was someone choosing something I made, out of everything at that entire market, wanting it in their home. Told Maya immediately, she laughed at how genuinely thrilled I was over it, said welcome to the addiction. I think she's right that this could become a real habit. Already thinking about what to make for the next one.

Still riding a little high from yesterday's market, sixty dollars and two sold pieces but the feeling's worth way more than that in some sense I can't quite articulate. Quiet Sunday recovering, canal walk in the evening, thinking about what a strange full year this has been so far and it's not even July yet.

Month's ending, and June somehow packed the move, Dario's dinner and that laugh I'll remember for years, and the market sale into just thirty days. Meridian steady and good underneath all of it. New apartment finally feels like mine now instead of just a place I recently dumped boxes into. Heading into July settled in a way I genuinely didn't expect to feel this soon after so much change.
